Mr. Chair, as the biggest troop contributors, the safety and security of UN peacekeeping personnel remains a primary concern for Nam. We emphasize the need to continue taking concrete concrete steps to ensuring reliable medical support for peacekeeping operations by improving access to adequate medical facilities, including mental health services, providing medical supplies, as well as in timely medical evacuation. We further call upon the Security Council to be more firm and use the full range of actions at its disposal to fight impunity in this context. We also note with concern the continued misinformation and disinformation campaigns against peacekeeping missions and peacekeepers, and recognize the danger these pose to the safety and security of peacekeepers. We urge the Secretariat and peacekeeping missions to strengthen their capacities and capabilities to counter misinformation, disinformation and hate speech, including by developing, executing and regularly reviewing and adapting their strategic communication plans. Ensuring that deployed contingents are fit for service, well-trained, and appropriately equipped is important in assessing performance. NAM emphasizes that this endeavor lays also on other factors, including leadership, performance and accountability at all levels, and eliminating caveats, whether declared or undeclared, which can, and actually do, severely impede implementation of missions mandates, are against the basic principle of equality and place an additional burden on peacekeepers who do not have any caveats. NAM supports efforts aimed at ensuring that all deployed personnel abide by the highest conduct standards and not commit or be involved in any acts that betray the trust in their mission and damage the image of peacekeeping and the UN. We call for United Nations intensified support to AU-led peacekeeping operations authorized by the Security Council, while taking duly into account the African Common Position as reflected in the African Consensus Paper.
